title: Elizabeth E Possible NDE 6646
content: I had been feeling pain in my left hip for fifteen years. I had told the doctors about my hip many times, but they always said it was just 'aging.' My hip had always gotten a lot of use, as I had always been very adventurous and active, canoeing the rivers of the Yukon, scuba diving all over the word, including Antarctica. I was one of the first women ever to scuba dive there in the year 2000. I had been an avid runner for twenty years, had traveled extensively and was now teaching Pilates, when I noticed a change in my hip, which had started to feel 'weird'. I thought it was a pinched nerve, but on Sunday in Sept 2012, I had four seizures in one day. One of those times, my left leg was stuck in a weird position and I fell over in extreme pain. The next day I went to my doctor and told her about this and demanded an MRI of my brain. One half-hour after my MRI, she told me I had a tumor the size of a lemon in my parietal lobe. I wanted the tumor out and everything was expedited at this point. Two days later, I had a ten-inch craniotomy, and had a biopsy, and they tried, but they could not remove all of the tumor because it was too deep. [med: Craniotomy: a surgical operation in which a bone flap is temporarily removed from the skull to access the brain.] I think I was in shock. They said it would take two weeks for the biopsy results. During the second surgery, I had an epiphany about Jesus. I felt enormous love from him and I felt horribly sorry I had not gotten closer to him during my life. When I would close my eyes, I would see a white light. I felt it was God looking at me and caring for me—and that Jesus was literally holding me. I felt safe, but the pain was horrible due to an allergy to morphine. My brother flew in, and he would sit by my side and pray. As I listened to him, I felt comfort, but still, the pain got in the way. There is more to this story, but I am home now, and I am in a watch-and-wait situation. I have brain cancer: Oligodendroglioma II [med. info: Type two is low grade, slow to change, and generally does not spread beyond the brain.] My life has changed. I am a better person because of the cancer. I have faith that I will be fine, even with the cancer in my head. God helped me and is helping me. I am fine.
